extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers of PLOS journals and the broader peer review community
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and practical resources for scientists and scholars who are preparing to review journal manuscripts (accepting/declining invitations, reading manuscripts, writing reviewer reports, and adhering to ethics/conflict rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: 10 Tips for Getting Started as a Peer Reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you thinking about being a peer reviewer but aren’t sure where to start? Are you concerned that you don’t have... (entry aimed at new reviewers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical starter advice for prospective reviewers (implicit criteria: readiness to review, basic expectations, how to begin). The page is positioned as an introductory how-to with tips for getting started.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to an Invitation (You've Been Invited to Review. Now What?)
rubrics_metrics.description: When you get an invitation to review a manuscript for a journal, what’s the first thing you should do? How do you... (guidance on deciding whether to accept an invitation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers initial steps after invitation: assessing fit/expertise, conflicts of interest, time commitment, and what to communicate when accepting or declining. (Page title implies these are the evaluative/decision criteria.)

rubrics_metrics.name: How to Read a Manuscript as a Peer Reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: What should you focus on when you review a scientific manuscript? This guide walks you through the process of reading a paper...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides reviewers on focus areas when reading a manuscript (e.g., key claims, methods, data, reproducibility, clarity). Serves as a reading checklist/process for evaluating a manuscript before writing comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to Write a Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.description: When you write a peer review for a manuscript, what should you include in your comments? What should you leave out? And...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides guidance on the content and tone of reviewer comments (what to include vs exclude), structure of reports, clarity, constructive feedback, and possibly confidentiality and professional language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Toolbox (PLOS Peer Review Toolbox)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PLOS Peer Review Toolbox is your source for best practices and practical tips to build your scientific peer review skillset. Delivered directly to your inbox, each issue is a new addition to your personal store of peer review and publishing know-how.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A curated set of best practices and tips — intended as ongoing professional development for reviewers. Implies evaluative dimensions such as staying current with best practices, continual skill-building, and applying recommended techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to Review a Manuscript Video
rubrics_metrics.description: This video guides peer reviewers through the process of reviewing a scientific manuscript from start to finish. Watch here, or follow along...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multimedia walkthrough of the manuscript-review process; useful for visual/stepwise demonstration of procedural criteria (what to check, in what order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Working on a peer review? Keep this checklist handy as you go through each step. Want a printable version of this checklist? Download....
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step-by-step checklist to use while performing a review — implies discrete criteria to verify (likely including scope, novelty, methods, statistics, data availability, ethical considerations, clarity). This entry points reviewers to a concise procedural evaluation tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Template
rubrics_metrics.description: Save or print this guide. Think about structuring your reviewer report like an upside-down pyramid. The most important information goes…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a recommended structure for reviewer reports (summary/major issues first, then details) — explicit guidance to place the most critical information at the top of the report and follow with supporting details and minor points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing Interests for Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: As a reviewer, you are expected to uphold the integrity of the peer review process. Sound like an intimidating amount of responsibility...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on recognising and declaring competing interests/conflicts of interest. Implies criteria for recusal or disclosure (e.g., personal, financial, institutional conflicts) and instructions on how to handle them during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics for Peer Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: As a reviewer, you have a crucial role in supporting research integrity in the peer review and publishing process. This guide outlines…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outlines ethical responsibilities of reviewers (confidentiality, fairness, avoiding misuse of privileged information, responsible tone). Functions as normative standards for appropriate reviewer behavior and evaluation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Data
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a growing appreciation of the importance of data storage, maintenance and sharing among the scientific research community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on evaluating data-related aspects of manuscripts: data availability, storage, reproducibility, and appropriate sharing/archiving practices. Reviewers are asked to assess whether data practices meet community/journal expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Peer Review
rubrics_metrics.description: What is Open Peer Review, and how is it different from other review models? Peer review is a pillar of scientific communication...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the model of open peer review and how it changes reviewer roles/visibility; implies criteria for transparency, openness of identities/reports, and considerations reviewers should take under open models.

rubrics_metrics.name: PLOS Reviewer Guidelines (per-journal guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you actively working on a review for PLOS? Select the relevant journal below for more detailed guidelines. [List of PLOS journals follows: PLOS Biology, PLOS Climate, PLOS Complex Systems, ... PLOS Water]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs reviewers to journal-specific guidance and standards (discipline- or journal-specific evaluation criteria, scope, and submission expectations). Implies that evaluation criteria may vary by journal and that reviewers should consult the relevant journal page for detailed rubrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training — How to Peer Review an Article (interactive training)
rubrics_metrics.description: Share the lessons of the Peer Review Center in a live, interactive training. Access tried-and-tested training modules, complete with slides and talking points, workshop activities, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers structured training modules for groups or instructors, including activities and materials to teach review skills; useful for standardising reviewer competence and applying the above criteria in practice.
